Fit the plane of intersection of a core to its outline

Source: R/cpi_pra.R
fit_intersection_plane.Rd

Fits a plane to the peripheral outline of a core by total least squares and finds the centre of the region the outline encloses. The plane and the centre are the reference for the Centripetality Index (CPI) and the Plane-Relative Angle (PRA) of cpi_pra_batch().

Usage

fit_intersection_plane(outline, K = 64)

Arguments

outline

The outline of one core: a numeric matrix or data frame with three columns (X, Y, Z), one point per row, ordered along the loop, as returned by read_outline_iges(). The loop is closed automatically if its last point differs from its first. A fitted intersection_plane object is returned unchanged.

K

Number of equally spaced points (by arc length) the plane is fitted to. Default 64.

Value

An object of class intersection_plane: a list with

centre

The centroid of the area enclosed by the outline (the centre against which CPI is measured).

normal

Unit normal of the fitted plane.

plane_centroid

The centroid of the K resampled points (a point on the plane).

basis

3 x 3 matrix whose rows are two in-plane axes and the normal (right-handed).

flatness

The smallest singular value of the resampled outline over the middle one: 0 for a perfectly flat outline; the larger it is, the more the single plane is an approximation.

rms_out_of_plane

Root mean square distance of the outline points from the plane.

diagonal

Length of the outline's bounding-box diagonal.

loop

The closed outline (first point repeated as the last).

Details

The plane is fitted to K points spaced equally along the outline, so that densely sampled stretches do not dominate the fit. The centre is the centroid of the enclosed area, not of the outline points: the loop is projected onto the fitted plane, the polygon centroid is taken there, and the result is lifted back.

The points must follow the outline in order. If the projected outline crosses itself, a warning is given: the points may be out of order, and the centre would then be wrong.

See also

read_outline_iges(), cpi_pra_batch(), plot_core()

Examples

# An ellipse tilted out of the XY plane
t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
loop <- cbind(30 * cos(t), 20 * sin(t), 3 * cos(t))
fit_intersection_plane(loop)
#> Warning: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> Warning: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> Warning: collapsing to unique 'x' values
#> <intersection_plane>
#>   centre (area centroid): 2.306e-15  8.783e-16  2.276e-16 
#>   normal:                 0.0995  2.204e-18  -0.995 
#>   flatness:               3.31e-17 
#>   rms out of plane:       5.575e-16 
#>   outline:                200 points, diagonal 72.36
